newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Most Brazilians against Cardoso's reelection.
newsitem.headline: Most Brazilians against Cardoso's reelection.

text.p: Most Brazilians are against President Fernando Henrique Cardoso seeking re-election in 1998, according to an opinion survey published on Sunday.
The Datafolha poll in the Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper found that 62 percent of people questioned in 12 cities were against re-election of the president.
Brazil has not allowed presidential re-election since the republic was established in 1889.

In the latest poll, 45 percent opposed re-election of a president in principle and another 17 percent thought the incumbent should not be allowed to benefit from any constitutional amendment passed by Congress allowing presidential re-election in the future.

The survey results compared with 46 percent against re-election in a Datafolha poll in August. The number of people who thought re-election should be allowed but that Cardoso should not run was the same at 17 percent.

Cardoso's allies have recently revived the debate about whether he should be allowed to seek a second term and the government is expected to send a proposal for a constitutional amendment to Congress after October's municipal elections.

The Datafolha survey showed that, if presidential elections were held today, Cardoso would be in a near deadheat with Workers Party candidate Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, with 23 percent and 21 percent of the vote respectively. Sao Paulo's Mayor Paulo Maluf trailed with 18 percent.
